solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sanction account, the thing's getting in red

indicators.note: the colour word is getting in between the account abbreviation and the thing, entering their pair

parts.note: it is the pronoun for 'the thing'; the 's is the verb 'is'
taken as written, the colour

explanation.surface: An accountant approves an account even though the business is going into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like being overdrawn, the opposite of credit; here it is just the colour, entered as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction someone or something is to give it official approval or authorisation, which is what accrediting does.

clue.text: Bell tower in quiet area between two rivers

indicators.note: the quiet sign and area letter sit between the two rivers, splitting them apart

parts.note: the Cam (in Cambridge) and the Nile
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A bell tower stands in a peaceful spot between two rivers, as in a college town.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a free-standing bell tower, typically Italian, beside a church.

clue.text: Fashionably liberal resort repels British

indicators.note: to repel is to drive away, so the resort's letter for British is pushed out

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A trendy, liberal seaside town turns away the British visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton, a seaside resort south of London, has a famously liberal reputation, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is an informal term for holding fashionably progressive or politically correct views.

clue.text: Fixer needs to prosper, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all of the phrase, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to do well is to prosper

explanation.surface: A political fixer needs to succeed, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden peg used to join or fix pieces of wood together, so it is a fixer.

clue.text: Turning obsessive over a barrel

indicators.note: turning round means the word for an obsessive is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is an obsessive enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: An obsessive turns over a barrel, or is caught over a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask or barrel for wine or beer.

clue.text: A sign of stress, getting right into wine

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the wine's name, landing inside it

parts.note: Macon is a French wine from the Maconnais in Burgundy

explanation.surface: Drinking wine as a sign that you are stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A macron marks a long vowel, which in prosody can signal a stressed syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The macron is the bar diacritic over a vowel marking length, used in verse to show a long or stressed syllable.

clue.text: Mother and girl finding way round doctor and chief steward

parts.note: ma is mother
Jo is a girl's name
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
O is round in shape
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Mother and daughter make their way to the doctor and the head steward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a containment signal, but it simply supplies the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A majordomo is the head servant who runs a great household, its principal steward.

clue.text: Amusing fellow worker who may be out of practice?

parts.note: CO, as in co-worker, means fellow or joint

parts.words: worker who may be out of practice
parts.note: a medic works in a medical practice and may be out of it on a home visit

explanation.surface: A colleague who is rusty from lack of practice is a source of amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of practice' suggests rusty, but here it means a doctor working away from the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic means relating to comedy, and so funny or amusing.

clue.text: Oval game unfortunately is last of the series

parts.note: O is oval in shape

indicators.note: the game has gone badly, so its letters come out in an unfortunate jumble

explanation.surface: A game at the Oval goes badly in the last match of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which feeds the sporting surface of a Test series.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of any series.

clue.text: Pleased with oneself getting sweets back

indicators.note: back means the word for sweets is read in reverse

parts.note: gums are chewy sweets such as wine gums

explanation.surface: Someone pleased with themselves after getting their sweets returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively self-satisfied.

clue.text: Trader's warm jacket

definitions.meaning: a merchant sailing ship, carrying trade goods
a windproof outer coat or windbreaker

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's cosy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large square-rigged merchant sailing ship and a windcheater-type jacket.

clue.text: Travel, going around with cine projector

indicators.note: the letters go round and come back in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Travelling about with a portable film projector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projector' looks like the cine kit, but it means something that juts out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a beam fixed at one end that projects out into space, as in a cantilever bridge.

clue.text: Millions supporting newly-formed native country

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes last
the letters of native are formed afresh into a new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Millions back a newly founded country of native people.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Truck departs with fish

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A lorry sets off carrying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low flat cart or truck, traditionally a brewer's delivery vehicle.

clue.text: The Spanish are able to pop back for summit

indicators.note: back means the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
can means are able
to nip is to pop, as in nip out to the shops

explanation.surface: Spanish climbers can nip back down from the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a high pointed peak, the summit of a mountain.

clue.text: Fine covering swindle involving key capital

indicators.note: the swindle wraps round and so involves the key and capital

parts.note: a con is a swindle
A is a musical key
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A fancy cover hides a scam centred on the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth covering for a horse, so a fine covering.

clue.text: Potter's second volume ultimately is magical

indicators.note: the second letter of the word Potter is picked out

parts.note: CC is cubic centimetres, a measure of volume
ult. is the dictionary abbreviation for ultimately

explanation.surface: The second Harry Potter book is ultimately all about magic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a Harry Potter volume, but 'Potter's second' just gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult describes the supernatural or magical, things beyond the natural world.

clue.text: Very old pine, something difficult to climb

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, so in a down entry the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a devil is something difficult, as in a devil of a job

explanation.surface: A very old pine tree is a hard thing to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone long-lived has lived to a great age, so is very old.

clue.text: Vessel unlikely to survive being in contact with a flying saucer?

definitions.text: Vessel unlikely to survive being in contact with a flying saucer?

parts.words: Vessel unlikely to survive being in contact with a flying saucer?
parts.note: the flying saucer is a hurled piece of crockery, and the cup that sits on it would break too

explanation.surface: A spacecraft would not last long alongside a UFO.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'flying saucer' suggest spacecraft, but these are china: a saucer thrown in a row takes its matching cup with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking cup for tea normally sits on a saucer, so it would be in contact with one.

clue.text: Fancy musical performance, one for queen

indicators.note: one goes in for queen, replacing it

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance
R is regina, queen
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A posh musical performance where one stands in for the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceit is a fanciful notion or an elaborate figure of speech, a fancy.

clue.text: Rubber prone to distort? Renew after stripping

indicators.note: distorting the word prone twists its letters out of shape
stripping removes the outer layers, leaving only the inner letters of the word Renew

explanation.surface: A rubber item liable to warp needs renewing after being stripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to distort' makes NEOPR from prone; 'stripping' takes the outer letters off Renew to leave ENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoprene is a synthetic rubber used in wetsuits and gaskets.

clue.text: Supporters missing the first game

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for supporters is left off

parts.note: brackets are wall supports for shelves

explanation.surface: Fans who miss the opening match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' looks like fans, but means shelf brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Rackets is a fast indoor ball game played with racquets, a forerunner of squash.

clue.text: Bog giving a home to river plant

indicators.note: the bog houses the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a fen is low marshy ground, a bog

explanation.surface: A marsh where a river feeds a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless plant with feathery fronds, common in damp places.

clue.text: Support rent getting left at the lowest level

indicators.note: in a down entry the lowest level is the bottom, so the letter goes to the end

parts.note: to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: Rent support for those left on the lowest income.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports an artist's canvas or a blackboard.

clue.text: Sheep fly round sierra? Likely to fall down

indicators.note: the sheep and fly together go round the sierra letter

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a hackle is an artificial fishing fly
S is sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Sheep flee round a mountain range and may well tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ramshackle is so badly made or neglected that it seems ready to collapse.

clue.text: Carnivore long among the last ones in South Africa

indicators.note: the yearning word sits among the two picked letters, between them
the final letters of the two words South and Africa

parts.note: to have a yen is to long for something

explanation.surface: A meat-eater with a long stay among South Africa's wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a flesh-eating African mammal, a scavenger and hunter.

clue.text: Seeming old and sober — about time

indicators.note: the sober word goes about the time letter, enclosing it

parts.note: sensible means level-headed, sober

explanation.surface: Apparently old and sober at about this time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or professed, as things seem rather than necessarily are.

clue.text: Prohibit nude, cancelling end of performance

indicators.note: cancelling removes the final letter picked out from the word for nude

parts.note: bare means nude

indicators.note: the last letter of the word performance

explanation.surface: Banning nudity, which ends the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar is to forbid or prohibit, as in barred from entry.

clue.text: European navy — not the answer to go green?

indicators.note: not means the answer letter is left out of the word navy

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Should a European navy go green, a question of environmental policy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'go green' suggests environmental policy, but means turning green with jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be green with jealousy is to covet, so going green is resenting another's luck.

clue.text: Something in wheat needs good clay with nitrogen

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Growing wheat requires good clay soil plus nitrogen fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

clue.text: Poem's rhythmic recitation spoken thus with extremes in delivery

indicators.note: spoken means the word for rhythmic recitation is heard, not seen, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: rap is rhythmic chanted speech over a beat
so means thus

indicators.note: the first and last letters of delivery

explanation.surface: A poem recited rhythmically, delivered with dramatic extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a rhapsody was an epic poem, or part of one, suitable for recitation.
